rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses continue the preceding discussion of diseased hearts, hypocrites, and those who apostatized after faith.
rows.anchor: بيان الآيات جارية على السياق السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānifan is an adverb for just before the present moment, or this very moment; it derives from anf, nose.
rows.anchor: آنفا اسم فاعل منصوب على الظرفية أو لكونه مفعولا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to unbelievers; listening means attending to the Prophet's Quran recitation and exposition of religious principles and laws.
rows.anchor: والمراد باستماعهم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إصغاؤهم إلى ما يتلوه من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the relative group by sense, while the earlier singular يستمع follows the relative's grammatical form.
rows.anchor: الضمير للموصول وجمع الضمير باعتبار المعنى كما أن إفراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge are companions who know God; the pronoun in their question refers to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المراد بالذين أوتوا العلم العلماء بالله من الصحابة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading takes the question as genuine inquiry: arrogance and desire kept them from understanding truth, as 4:78 also says.
rows.anchor: قيل للاستعلام حقيقة لأن استغراقهم في الكبر والغرور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second reported reading is mockery; al-Tabatabai considers this interpretation plausible.
rows.anchor: وقيل للاستهزاء، وقيل للتحقير كأن القول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third reading is contempt: they imply the speech is full of falsehoods and has no coherent meaning; the author says each reading has a basis.
rows.anchor: وقيل للتحقير كأن القول لكونه مشحونا بالأباطيل

words: أولئك الذين طبع الله على قلوبهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first clause identifies them and the second restates it explanatorily; following desires signals a sealed heart, while one pure in original nature grasps divine truths readily.
rows.anchor: تعريف بعد تعريف فهو كعطف التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance counters the misguidance that accompanies a sealed heart: it means submitting to sound innate nature and following truth.
rows.anchor: المراد بالاهتداء ما يقابل الضلال الملازم للطبع على القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases their guidance by raising their degree of faith; guidance and faith have multiple degrees.
rows.anchor: زيادة هداهم من الله سبحانه رفعه تعالى درجة إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa counters following desires and means scrupulous avoidance of God's prohibitions and sins.
rows.anchor: المراد بالتقوى ما يقابل اتباع الأهواء وهو الورع عن محارم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase in guidance perfects knowledge, while granting taqwa perfects action.
rows.anchor: زيادة الهدى راجع إلى تكميلهم في ناحية العلم وإيتاء التقوى إلى تكميلهم في ناحية العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, sealing signifies loss of perfected knowledge and following desires loss of righteous action; this does not conflict with reading the second clause as explanatory of the first.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا ينافي ما قدمنا أن اتباع الأهواء كعطف التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Looking means waiting; ashrāṭ are signs, named from conditions on which something depends because their occurrence signals it.
rows.anchor: والأشراط جمع شرط بمعنى العلامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ defines a shaʿb as a large human community such as Rabia or Mudar, and a tribe as a subdivision such as Tamim within Mudar.
rows.anchor: الشعوب جمع شعب بالكسر فالسكون وهو على ما في المجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tribe is a division below a people, such as Tamim within Mudar.
rows.anchor: والقبائل جمع قبيلة وهي دون الشعب كتميم من مضر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view reverses the hierarchy: peoples are below tribes and are named for branching.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشعوب دون القبائل وسميت بها لتشعبها

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines a shaʿb as a tribe branching from one community and explains the root through a valley's gathering and dispersal, so the verb can mean unite or divide.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الشعب القبيلة المنشعبة من حي واحد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss identifies peoples with non-Arabs and tribes with Arabs; the author says this seems reducible to one of the preceding definitions.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشعوب العجم والقبائل العرب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Commentators read male and female as Adam and Eve: all people share the same parents irrespective of color or ethnicity.
rows.anchor: ذكر المفسرون أن الآية مسوقة لنفي التفاخر بالأنساب

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: On that reading, peoples and tribes exist for mutual recognition and the social ties and dealings that sustain community, not for lineage-based boasting.
rows.anchor: لا لكرامة لبعضكم على بعض بل لأن تتعارفوا فيعرف بعضكم بعضا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reads male and female generally and treats the verse as abolishing every class distinction, since everyone is born from a man and a woman.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالذكر والأنثى مطلق الرجل والمرأة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On the broader reading, divinely created differences among peoples and tribes serve recognition and social cohesion, not superiority or virtue.
rows.anchor: والاختلاف الحاصل بالشعوب والقبائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says recognition does not clearly follow from abolishing all class distinctions, since the verse specifically condemns lineage pride.
rows.anchor: واعترض عليه بأن الآية مسوقة لنفي التفاخر بالأنساب وذمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that lineage is one form of class distinction: pride can be rejected because all share Adam and Eve, or because everyone is born from two people.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يناقش فيه أن الاختلاف في الأنساب من مصاديق الاختلاف الطبقاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the clause clearly condemns lineage pride, the Adam-and-Eve reading is stronger; otherwise the broader reading is preferable for its inclusive scope.
rows.anchor: إن كان ظاهرا في ذم التفاخر بالأنساب فأول الوجهين أوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains honor with God: human differences exist for recognition and cooperation, not boasting, enslavement, exploitation, group arrogance, or corruption that destroys life.
rows.anchor: استئناف مبين لما فيه الكرامة عند الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People naturally seek distinction, but those attached to worldly life treat wealth, beauty, lineage, and status as honor and pursue them to boast over others.
rows.anchor: الإنسان مجبول على طلب ما يتميز به من غيره ويختص به من بين أقرانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These material distinctions are illusory and bring no real honor; instead they lead to ruin and misery.
rows.anchor: وهذه مزايا وهمية لا تجلب لهم شيئا من الشرف والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Real honor leads to true happiness, eternal good life near God; taqwa is the sole means to afterlife happiness, followed by worldly happiness.
rows.anchor: والشرف الحقيقي هو الذي يؤدي الإنسان إلى سعادته الحقيقية وهو الحياة الطيبة الأبدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports this with 8:67, where God wills the hereafter, and 2:197, which calls taqwa the best provision.
rows.anchor: تريدون عرض الدنيا والله يريد الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's chosen goal of taqwa creates no competition among its adherents, unlike imagined worldly goals such as wealth, leadership, beauty, fame, and ancestry.
rows.anchor: وهذه البغية والغاية التي اختارها الله بعلمه غاية للناس لا تزاحم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge and awareness reinforce the verse: He chose real honor knowingly, while humanly chosen worldly adornments are false and imaginary.
rows.anchor: فيه تأكيد لمضمون الآية وتلويح إلى أن الذي اختاره الله كرامة للناس كرامة حقيقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast between worldly adornment and the real afterlife also appears in 29:64.
rows.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا إلا لهو ولعب وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse obliges people to pursue the ends their Lord commands and choose taqwa, the goal He selected and guides them toward.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن من الواجب على الناس أن يتبعوا في غايات الحياة أمر ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing verses address some Bedouins who claimed faith and treated their profession as a favor to the Prophet; the wording does not mean all Bedouins.
rows.anchor: وسياق نقل قولهم وأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يجيبهم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen of the heavens and earth may mean what is hidden within them, or more broadly what is within them and beyond them.
rows.anchor: والمراد بغيب السماوات والأرض ما فيها من الغيب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Muqatil that the verse was revealed about Banu Tamim mocking Bilal, Salman, Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Ibn Fuhayra, and Salim.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مقاتل في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says the verse concerned Thabit ibn Qays: after crossing people's necks, he insulted a man by invoking his mother's pre-Islamic nickname; the man bowed in shame.
rows.anchor: فنكس الرجل رأسه حياء فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports from Anas that the verse concerned the Prophet's wives mocking Umm Salama's trailing white garment; Aisha drew Hafsa's attention to it.
rows.anchor: عن أنس. وذلك أنها ربطت حقويها بسبيبة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A second explanation from al-Hasan says the women mocked Umm Salama for being short, gesturing to indicate her height.
rows.anchor: وأشارت بيدها أنها قصيرة. عن الحسن

rows.speaker: أبو جبيرة بن الضحاك
rows.claim: Abu Jubayra reports that among Banu Salima, people had several names and objected when called by a disliked one; al-Hakim graded the report sound.
rows.anchor: والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن أبي جبيرة بن الضحاك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that two travel companions disparaged Salman while he slept and ate their provisions; they sent him to the Prophet to request relish, beginning the account continued next.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن السدي أن سلمان الفارسي كان مع رجلين في سفر

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Diya al-Maqdisi transmits from Anas that Abu Bakr and Umar called their sleeping servant a heavy sleeper and sent him for relish; the Prophet said they had eaten their companion's flesh.
rows.anchor: وفيه أخرج الضياء المقدسي عن أنس قال كانت العرب يخدم بعضها بعضا في الأسفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai judges the two travel stories to be one incident: the first report names Abu Bakr and Umar as the men, the second names Salman as the servant.
rows.anchor: أقول الظاهر أن القصة الموردة في الروايتين واحدة

rows.speaker: جوامع الجامع
rows.claim: A corroborating version says Abu Bakr and Umar sent Salman to Usama for food and disparaged both men; the Prophet said they had wronged Salman and Usama.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا ما عن جوامع الجامع قال وروي أن أبا بكر وعمر بعثا سلمان

rows.speaker: الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Rida declines to name a poet as the Iraqi or al-Atahiya, reasoning that the man may dislike the label in light of the ban on offensive nicknames.
rows.anchor: سمعت الرضا عليه السلام يوما ينشد

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali advises interpreting a brother's conduct and words in the best available light until evidence changes that judgment.
rows.anchor: قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في كلام له ضع أمر أخيك على أحسنه

rows.speaker: عليه السلام
rows.claim: Ali says that in a righteous age, suspecting someone with no visible offense is unjust; in a corrupt age, assuming the best is self-deception.
rows.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة وقال عليه السلام إذا استولى الصلاح على الزمان وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sayings do not conflict: one concerns the act of suspecting, the other concerns putting suspicion into practice.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايتان غير متعارضتين فالثانية ناظرة إلى نفس الظن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Khisal transmits from the Prophet that backbiting is worse than adultery because the repentant adulterer may be forgiven, while the backbiter must first be released by the victim.
rows.anchor: عن أسباط بن محمد بإسناده إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur transmits a parallel Prophetic wording from Abu Sa'id and Jabir: the backbiter is not forgiven until the victim forgives; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد وجابر عنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Kafi transmits through al-Sukuni from Abu Abd Allah that the Prophet compares backbiting's damage to a Muslim's religion with an eating illness consuming the body.
rows.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده إلى السكوني عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Asked how to expiate backbiting, the Prophet says to seek God's forgiveness for the person backbitten, as one mentioned that person.
rows.anchor: عن حفص بن عمر عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi glosses peoples as non-Arabs and tribes as Arabs; al-Majmaʿ attributes the same report to al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: ونسبه في مجمع البيان إلى الصادق عليه السلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In a Farewell address during the Days of Tashriq, the Prophet says all share one Lord and father and no Arab, non-Arab, or color group has precedence except through taqwa; witnesses should inform the absent.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports that the Prophet married Miqdad ibn al-Aswad to Dubāʿa bint al-Zubayr to lower marriage barriers, model the practice, and show nobility rests on taqwa.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بكر الحضرمي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked what nobility is, Abu Abd Allah answers: taqwa.
rows.anchor: عن جميل بن دراج قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام فما الكرم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports from Abu Abd Allah that Islam comes before faith: inheritance and marriage follow Islam, while reward is based on faith.
rows.anchor: عن يونس بن يعقوب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث قال إن الإسلام قبل الإيمان

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Khisal reports from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that Islam and faith differ: every believer is Muslim, but not every Muslim is a believer.
rows.anchor: عن الأعمش عن جعفر بن محمد عليه السلام في حديث

words: بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labs means confusion; new creation transforms the worldly order into another realm without death or extinction, where the blessed have joy without sorrow and the wretched face unrelieved torment.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخلق الجديد تبديل نشأتهم الدنيا من نشأة أخرى ذات نظام آخر

words: بل هم في لبس من خلق جديد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God first created and governed the heavens, earth, and all within them with knowledge and power, recreating them poses no incapacity; the disbelievers remain confused and unable to believe.
rows.anchor: إذا كنا خلقنا العالم بسمائه وأرضه وما فيهما ودبرناه أحسن تدبير لأول مرة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines waswasa as a bad, fleeting thought, deriving it from waswas, the sound of jewelry or a faint whisper.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الوسوسة الخطرة الرديئة وأصله من الوسواس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the human means his ongoing, changing existence, not only his initial formation; every creature that persists continually depends on its Lord.
rows.anchor: والمراد بخلق الإنسان وجوده المتدرج المتحول خلقا بعد خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present-tense knowledge clause signals continuity alongside the past-tense but continuing act of creation.
rows.anchor: وهو فعل مضارع مسوق للدلالة على الاستمرار على قوله

words: ونحن أقرب إليه من حبل الوريد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement of nearness likewise conveys permanence and continuity for as long as the human exists.
rows.anchor: مفيد للثبوت والدوام والاستمرار باستمرار وجود الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse links to the argument from God's knowledge and power in first creation in 50:6 and to the preceding doubt about a new creation in 50:15.
rows.anchor: اتصال بما تقدم من الاحتجاج على علمه وقدرته تعالى في الخلق الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes God's direct knowledge of the human and, through guardian angels, knowledge of his acts; awareness of inner whispering signals knowledge of all outward and inward states.
rows.anchor: فهي في سياق يذكر قدرته على الإنسان بخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hidden thought includes a skeptic's doubt about resurrection: how can a person be raised after death has scattered the body into indistinguishable dust?
rows.anchor: ومما توسوس به الشبهة في أمر المعاد كيف يبعث الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here mā is a relative pronoun, the pronoun in bihi refers to it, and the preposition means instrument or cause.
rows.anchor: عائد إليه والباء للآلة أو للسببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse attributes whispering to the self rather than Satan, though Satan also whispers, because it discusses God's encompassing knowledge of the human and his innermost thoughts.
rows.anchor: ونسب الوسوسة إلى النفس دون الشيطان وإن كانت منسوبة إليه أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warid is a blood-carrying vein distributed through the body; another view identifies it as the vein in the throat. It is called a cord by comparison, and the genitive is explanatory.
rows.anchor: الوريد عرق متفرق في البدن فيه مجاري الدم

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is nearer to a person than the vein running among his organs inside the body, so He fully knows him and his inner thoughts.
rows.anchor: المخالط لأعضائه المستقر في داخل بدنه فكيف لا نعلم به

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The familiar image is an easy approximation for ordinary understanding, while God's actual nearness is vastly greater.
rows.anchor: وهذا تقريب للمقصود بجملة ساذجة يسهل تلقيها لعامة الأفهام

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the human a soul and ordered its effects; He mediates between the soul and itself and between it and its actions, nearer than anything one can posit, even the self.
rows.anchor: فهو الواسطة بينها وبين نفسها وبينها وبين آثارها وأفعالها

words: وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This subtle account of divine nearness is comparable to 8:24, which says God comes between a person and his heart.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه بوجه قوله { إن الله يحول بين المرء وقلبه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two receivers are the two angels assigned to a person, who receive his deeds and preserve them in writing.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالمتلقيان على ما يفيده السياق الملكان الموكلان على الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase elides a second sitting angel: one sits at the right and one at the left; these are the person's own sides, and qaʿīd means seated.
rows.anchor: تقديره عن اليمين قعيد وعن الشمال قعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes idh with an omitted verb, meaning remember when the angels receive; this adds knowledge through the recorders to God's immediate, unmediated knowledge.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه متعلق بمحذوف والتقدير اذكر إذ يتلقى المتلقيان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view attaches idh to the preceding assertion of nearness, meaning God is nearer while the two angels receive the person's deeds.
rows.anchor: وقيل الظرف متعلق بقوله في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the omitted-verb reading because the context, especially the next verse, makes divine knowledge through nearness and through angels independently intended.
rows.anchor: ولعل الوجه السابق أوفق للسياق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view makes idh causal, using the angels' receiving as the reason for God's knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل { إذ } تعليلية تعلل علمه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the causal reading as unlikely Quranic argumentation: God's knowledge would not be inferred from the angels' knowledge, preservation, and writing.
rows.anchor: وفيه أن من البعيد من مذاق القرآن أن يستدل على علمه تعالى بعلم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Right and left illustrate the angels' positions and represent the sides of good and evil, to which good and bad deeds respectively belong.
rows.anchor: تمثيل لموقعهما من الإنسان

words: ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafẓ literally means throwing and is metaphorically used for speaking; raqīb is guardian, and ʿatīd means prepared and ready to remain with the matter.
rows.anchor: اللفظ الرمي سمي به التكلم بنوع من التشبيه

words: ما يلفظ من قول إلا لديه رقيب عتيد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse emphasizes the recording angels' surveillance of speech; after the two receivers, it singles out speech from the broader class for special attention.
rows.anchor: الآية تذكر مراقبة الكتبة للإنسان فيما يتكلم به من كلام
